reasons: Weak convergence of the baseline empirical measures controls empirical conditional moments only when those moment functions are continuous and bounded on a common compact set containing the actual triangular array. The frozen smoothness condition is restricted to the support of the limiting measure and does not control off-support array points approaching that support.

narrow: Constant rank and oracle smoothness prove the quantile, density, coarea, and curvature conclusions, but the frozen dependencies impose no continuity condition on the efficient-information map. Therefore unconditional continuity of the final trace functional is stronger than the premises; the corrected claim makes precisely that last implication conditional.
The narrowed claim names outcome moments and uses exact Horvitz--Thompson centering, so its free-symbol list and proof dependency must be updated atomically.

narrow: The frozen class requires only a memberwise finite outcome bound and fixes no common numerical envelope. Rescaling any admissible outcome family by an arbitrary finite constant preserves the qualitative model conditions and trace-normalized oracle action but multiplies design risks by the square of that constant, so the supremum over all model members is infinite. The replacement gives the exact computable inequality supported by the design.

narrow: Han and Deng's Assumption 3 requires the full \(F\)-dimensional projected factorial covariance and its limit to be nonsingular. The frozen oracle-rank condition requires only a common positive rank \(r_G\), and does not impose \(r_G=F\) or nonvanishing unnormalized projected covariance. Thus the un-intersected inclusion is stronger than the frozen premises. The replacement leaves the published class unchanged and restricts the left-hand side to a subclass of the original realization class; the proof certifies strictness with an explicit Han--Deng array excluded by the frozen baseline bound.

narrow: The exact symmetry and pooled-law reductions are finite combinatorial consequences of the frozen design. The original first-order limit sentence has no triangular-array Lindeberg, limiting covariance, or cited limit-theorem node among its dependencies, so it is not a theorem under the stated premises and is removed rather than assumed.

verdict.note: High-effort math adjudication approved all five changes as faithful and non-laundering. Merge the PR; the rejected global-sharp-pilot item is statement-identical and its dependency-only change will be committed immediately after the certificate lemma lands.
